subject: Automotive & EVs
title: India's EV Opportunity
description: A short lesson to help you apply India's EV Opportunity.

hook.text: India has 1.4 billion people and choking urban pollution. EVs could help—if they're affordable.

buildup.text: Most Indian vehicles are two-wheelers and small cars. Cheap electric scooters are already surging.

discovery.text: Ola Electric and Tata Motors are leading the push with affordable models under $15,000.

twist.text: India's power grid still runs mostly on coal. EVs there shift tailpipe emissions to power plants.

climax.text: But India is also investing in solar. As the grid cleans up, EVs become greener automatically.

punchline.text: India's EV story starts on two wheels, not four.

quiz.question: What type of EV is growing fastest in India?

details.summary: India is emerging as a major EV market driven by two-wheeler and three-wheeler electrification, government subsidies, and air quality crises in major cities, though car electrification still lags behind China and Europe.
details.whyItMatters: India's potential EV market is enormous. With 1.4 billion people and worsening urban air pollution, the country's electrification path could have massive global environmental and manufacturing impacts.
takeaways: Electric two-wheelers are leading India's EV transition
Government subsidies through FAME schemes support EV adoption
Air quality crises in Delhi and other cities drive urgency

faq.question: Why are two-wheelers leading India's EV transition?
faq.answer: Two-wheelers account for over 70 percent of Indian vehicle sales. They are affordable, have short daily ranges suited to current battery technology, and are easier to charge than cars in India's space-constrained urban environments.

faq.question: Can India build its own EV industry?
faq.answer: India is investing in domestic battery manufacturing through companies like Ola Electric and Tata. The government's production-linked incentive scheme aims to attract global battery makers to build factories in India.
